A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Injective Flows for Star-like Manifolds. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original density-reconstruction experiments, synthetic Bayesian regression, comparisons with MCMC, and portfolio results in Section 5 and Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical applications and adds original runtime and exact-versus-approximate Jacobian experiments in Section 5.1 and Appendix Figure 10.

M1.justification: The angle flow, radial embedding, spherical-to-Cartesian transformation, exact determinant formula and reverse-KL training objective remain unchanged. Expanded spline explanations and newly documented numerical safeguards do not establish a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Synthetic coverage expands to uniform-density learning on an lp manifold with p=0.5, and the spherical checkerboard example is replaced by a sinusoidal density on a deformed sphere. The regression, conjugate mixing-model and 10-stock, 200-step portfolio coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds direct computational comparators absent from v2: explicit determinant computation using Eq. (2), and otherwise identical flows trained with Hutchinson-estimated Jacobian gradients. The latter use the implementation attributed to Sorrenson et al. (2024), with several estimator sample counts. These substantially extend comparison beyond the retained prior-choice and MCMC experiments.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 introduces controlled comparisons across dimensions 3, 10, 50 and 100 and Gaussian estimator sample counts 1, 10, 50 and 100, subject to the stated dimensionality bound. Both training variants use exact Jacobians at evaluation; metrics include log-density MSE, energy-distance MMD, Sinkhorn divergence and runtime. The third 3D target also changes from 2 sin(6θ) sin(6ϕ) to sin(4θ) sin(4ϕ). Existing regression and MCMC settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 3 and 10 directly test the importance of exact Jacobian training by holding the flow architecture fixed and varying the approximation sample count and dimension. They assess density accuracy, sample quality and computational cost. v3 also adds an empirical scaling analysis of determinant computation; v2's prior-sensitivity and MCMC analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 reports 20 repetitions for the new determinant-timing experiment and displays variability in the added comparisons. This does not establish increased repetition of earlier experiments. Existing 95% posterior intervals remain unchanged; training-run counts and the definitions of the new error bars are not fully specified.

E6.justification: New results report fitted runtime scaling of approximately d^2.96 for explicit computation versus d^1.81 for the proposed approach, and better density and sample-quality scores with exact Jacobian training. The first two 3D examples retain MSEs 0.013 and 0.011. The old checkerboard MSE of 0.024 disappears when that experiment is replaced by a qualitatively evaluated deformed-sphere example. Bayesian and portfolio results are retained.

T1.justification: Sections 2 and 3.2 add the relaxed change-of-variables condition of a diffeomorphism almost everywhere and explain why measure-zero coordinate singularities preserve the density calculation. Theorem 1, its quadratic-complexity argument, and the definitions, lemmas and proofs in Appendices A.1–A.4 otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: exact, efficient injective flows for star-like manifolds and applications to objective Bayesian inference and mixing models. The conclusion adds empirical support for efficiency and exact-Jacobian importance, both already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: v3 clarifies the consequences of coordinate singularities for exact density evaluation and numerical stability, and explicitly motivates its focus on variational inference through the codimension-one restriction. Existing dimensionality and expressivity limitations remain. Learning the radial function from observations is still discussed in Appendix A.5.

D1.justification: v3 documents small angular offsets near singularities and expands the circular-spline implementation description, including rational-quadratic segments and periodic boundaries. It identifies the approximation implementation and specifies Sinkhorn blur=0.05. Existing architecture sizes, Adam settings, GPU information and FlowConductor access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Kothari et al. (2021) and Munkres and Spivak (1965), and removes Cayton (2005) and Krantz and Parks (2008). The related-work discussion and positioning against approximate injective flows remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 becomes Further Details and Limitations with separate explanatory paragraphs, and a new Section 5.1 precedes the existing applications. Appendix mixing-model material moves from A.6.4 to A.7.1. There are localized prose edits and updated publication headers, while most narrative and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the runtime/accuracy panels in Figure 3 and sample-quality/runtime panels in Figure 10, and redraws the third illustrative-density example. Figure 1 is smaller, and retained figures are renumbered or relocated, including the final appendix plots. The overall visual format and most existing displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 closes a central empirical gap: v2 argued for efficient, exact Jacobians without directly testing their computational advantage and training benefit against approximation. Section 5.1 and Figure 10 add controlled evidence on scaling, density accuracy and sample quality while retaining the original applications and proofs. The replacement 3D example loses quantitative scoring, and replication details remain incomplete, but these limitations are outweighed by substantially stronger evidence for the paper's central contribution.
